source.title: Rethinking AI in Knowledge Work: From Assistant to Tool for Thought
facts: Microsoft Research distinguishes assistant mode, centered on speed and completion, from a tool-for-thought mode centered on depth, judgment, sense-making, and creativity.
The article summarizes mixed findings, including risks of narrower ideas, reduced critical thinking, and weaker retention in some settings.
Its prototype explorations include surfacing tensions, offering alternate interpretations, and asking probing questions.

centralThesis: AI should not only complete work for people. When understanding and judgment are part of the deliverable, the workflow should expose tension, preserve the reasoning trail, and leave consequential trade-offs with an accountable person.

P0: Define the human thinking to preserve
P1: Preserve initial judgment and turning points
Bind claims to primary evidence and counterevidence
P3: Treat more output as proof of learning
Accept the AI answer as the default conclusion

reusableArtifact: Thought-preservation card: human goal, AI role, evidence action, and human gate.

chapters.title: Name the thinking at risk
chapters.promise: The first step is not choosing a model. It is naming the kind of human thinking this task is supposed to preserve.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, define the human thinking this task must preserve.
Second, treat hypotheses, counterexamples, and trade-offs as high-risk outsourcing points.
Third, leave a minimal independent attempt before you read the AI answer.

chapters.title: Make AI expose tension
chapters.promise: The second step is not asking AI to sound more certain. Ask it to expose the tensions hiding inside the problem.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, keep conflicting goals visible at the same time.
Second, compare at least two interpretations that could reasonably be true.
Third, pursue only questions that can materially change the decision.

chapters.title: Keep reasoning visible
chapters.promise: The third step is keeping the reasoning trail on the table instead of saving only the final answer.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, preserve the initial judgment and every meaningful revision.
Second, separate facts, sources, and inference in the record.
Third, test understanding by restating the reasoning without the answer.

chapters.title: Reserve human judgment
chapters.promise: The fourth step is deciding which gates require a human to make the final judgment.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, keep value choices and irreversible decisions behind a human gate.
Second, approval must include evidence, uncertainty, and consequences.
Third, concentrate human attention on the moments that change direction.

chapters.title: Use the thought card
chapters.promise: Finally, compress the method into a four-field thought-preservation card.

recaps.narration: Chapter recap. First, state the human learning and judgment goal.
Second, define the AI role, evidence action, and prohibited zone.
Third, finish the trade-off at a named human judgment gate.
recaps.screenText: Finish at a named human gate

factBoundaries: The article summarizes mixed research evidence; it does not claim that every use of AI weakens judgment.
The prototypes demonstrate design directions, not universal proof across all knowledge work.
The thought-preservation card is this episode's practical synthesis, not an official Microsoft template.
inference: Organizing the principles into the four fields of human goal, AI role, evidence action, and human gate is a workflow inference for viewers.
